summary: Scans a byte buffer from a1 for a2 bytes looking for the n-th backslash (0x5C = 92) character, where n is a3. Returns the position of the n-th backslash as an offset from a1, returns 0 immediately when n is zero, and returns -1 when fewer than n backslashes exist in the range. Called by sub_563870.

operations.description: If a3 (count to find) is zero, returns 0 immediately without scanning.
Sets v5 to the end of the scan range a1 + a2 and initializes the scan pointer v4 to a1.
Iterates while the scan pointer v4 has not reached the end v5.
When the current byte *v4 equals 92 (backslash), decrements the remaining count v3.
Advances the scan pointer v4 by one byte.
Returns v4 - a1 (the position offset) as soon as the remaining count v3 reaches zero, i.e. the n-th backslash has been passed.
After the loop, returns -1 when the remaining count v3 is still nonzero (fewer than n backslashes present), otherwise returns the final position v4 - a1.
